sentences.en: Episode 54, Programming for the GPU.
sentences.zh: 第 54 期，GPU 编程。

sentences.en: Take it away, Patrick.
sentences.zh: 请开始吧，帕特里克。

sentences.en: We're here today with Mark Harris from NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了来自英伟达的马克·哈里斯。

sentences.en: Mark, why don't you go ahead and introduce yourself.
sentences.zh: 马克，不妨先自我介绍一下。

sentences.en: Tell us a little bit about what you do with NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 跟我们聊聊你在英伟达负责什么工作。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so my title at NVIDIA is Chief Technologist for GPU Computing Software.
sentences.zh: 好，我在英伟达的头衔是 GPU 计算软件首席技术专家。

sentences.en: And my role is kind of twofold.
sentences.zh: 我的职责大致分为两个方面。

sentences.en: One is inward-facing and one is outward-facing.
sentences.zh: 一个是面向内部的，另一个是面向外部的。

sentences.en: So my inward-facing role is to help define our software strategy for computing at NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 面向内部的职责是帮助定义英伟达计算软件战略。

sentences.en: And so that's for things like CUDA programming, which we'll talk about more, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 也就是 CUDA 编程之类的技术，我们后面有机会还会深入探讨。

sentences.en: And the other aspect is the external-facing role, which is a little bit of evangelism, giving talks at conferences such as the GPU Technology Conference.
sentences.zh: 另一个方面是面向外部的职责，有点像技术布道，比如在 GPU 技术大会等会议上发表演讲。

sentences.en: And I also run a blog called Parallel for All, which is on NVIDIA.
sentences.zh: 我还运营一个名为 Parallel for All 的博客，托管在英伟达官网上。

sentences.en: Hopefully you guys can drop a link after the show recording.
sentences.zh: 希望各位在节目播出后能放个链接。

sentences.en: And on that blog, it's a developer blog written by developers for developers.
sentences.zh: 这个博客是一个由开发者为开发者撰写的开发者博客。

sentences.en: And it's a deeply technical blog about parallel programming and GPU programming.
sentences.zh: 它是一个专注于并行编程和 GPU 编程的深度技术博客。

sentences.en: So can you maybe just give us a little bit of background, what NVIDIA is, what they do as a company?
sentences.zh: 那么你能不能大概介绍一下背景，英伟达是一家什么样的公司，他们是做什么的？

sentences.en: I mean, I think most people have heard of them, but they just think of, well, I guess people don't go to Best Buy anymore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得大多数人都听说过他们，但他们只觉得……好吧，我猜现在人们也不怎么去百思买（Best Buy）了。

sentences.en: But you go to Amazon or Newegg or whatever the international equivalent is.
sentences.zh: 但你会去亚马逊、新蛋网或者其他什么国际同类网站。

sentences.en: I still go to Best Buy.
sentences.zh: 我还是会去百思买。

sentences.en: Sorry, Best Buy.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，百思买。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, anyways, kind of tell us who NVIDIA is, like what they do, and why CUDA is a thing.
sentences.zh: 总之，请跟我们讲讲英伟达是谁，他们是做什么的，以及为什么会有 CUDA 这种技术。

sentences.en: Okay, so, well, what is NVIDIA?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么，英伟达是什么？

sentences.en: NVIDIA is a visual computing company.
sentences.zh: 英伟达是一家视觉计算公司。

sentences.en: And what that means is that we focus on building solutions for all aspects of visual computing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们专注于为视觉计算的各个方面构建解决方案。

sentences.en: We call ourselves the inventors of the GPU.
sentences.zh: 我们自称为 GPU 的发明者。

sentences.en: That's the graphics processing unit.
sentences.zh: 也就是图形处理器。

sentences.en: I think NVIDIA coined that term back in like 1999 with the first GeForce product.
sentences.zh: 我想英伟达在 1999 年左右推出第一款 GeForce 产品时就创造了这个词。

sentences.en: And most consumers would be familiar with, especially gamers, would be familiar with our GeForce GPUs,
sentences.zh: 大多数消费者都会熟悉，特别是游戏玩家会熟悉我们的 GeForce GPU，

sentences.en: which are graphics cards for making your game's graphics look amazing and run really faSt.
sentences.zh: 它们是用来让你的游戏画面看起来惊艳且运行极快的显卡。

sentences.en: But GPUs are used in a variety of computations.
sentences.zh: 但 GPU 也被用于各种计算。

sentences.en: And so we have four kind of focused business areas.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有四个重点业务领域。

sentences.en: And those are gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive.
sentences.zh: 分别是游戏、专业可视化、数据中心和汽车。

sentences.en: And visual computing or parallel computing are really important in all four of those.
sentences.zh: 视觉计算或并行计算在这四个领域都极为重要。

sentences.en: And it turns out that GPUs are very useful and good at accelerating those computations.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，GPU 在加速这些计算方面非常有用且出色。

sentences.en: So the obvious ones are gaming, because the GPU was designed for computer graphics and also professional visualization.
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见的领域是游戏，因为 GPU 本就是为计算机图形学设计的，还有专业可视化。

sentences.en: But the area I work in is data center and parallel computing.
sentences.zh: 但我工作的领域是数据中心和并行计算。

sentences.en: So, you know, GPUs, it turns out, are great at parallel computing because graphics is parallel.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，事实证明 GPU 非常擅长并行计算，因为图形本身就是并行的。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I don't know how much detail you want me to go into about the history of that.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，我不知道你想让我详细讲多少关于这方面的历史。

sentences.en: Well, maybe, I mean, a simple way of saying it is that with graphics, you're trying to do two things.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许，简单来说就是，在处理图形时，你主要在做两件事。

sentences.en: You're trying to figure out where a bunch of triangles are in space.
sentences.zh: 你得算出空间里有一堆什么三角形。

sentences.en: And then you're also trying to draw sort of a bunch of pixels on the screen.
sentences.zh: 然后你还得在屏幕上画出一堆像素。

sentences.en: And in both cases, they're kind of embarrassingly parallel.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，它们都具有极高的可并行性。

sentences.en: Like, you have many triangles, and they can all be discovered, rendered, you know, located independently.
sentences.zh: 比如，你有许多三角形，它们都可以被独立发现、渲染和定位。

sentences.en: And you have many pixels that can all be processed more or less independently.
sentences.zh: 而且你有很多像素，或多或少都可以被独立处理。

sentences.en: And so that makes the GPU kind of, like, ideal for doing a lot of these things in parallel, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这使得 GPU 成为并行处理大量此类任务的理想选择，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you have millions of pixels to shade in every frame, and you're running, you know, 60 frames a second or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你每一帧都有数百万个像素要着色，而且你还要保持每秒 60 帧左右的运行速率。

sentences.en: So, and triangles, I guess modern games probably have hundreds of thousands to millions of triangles per frame, too.
sentences.zh: 至于三角形，我想现代游戏每帧大概也有数十万到数百万个三角形。

sentences.en: So you're getting to the point of having, you know, pixel size or sub-pixel triangles.
sentences.zh: 所以你已经达到了拥有像素大小或亚像素大小三角形的程度。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so back in the day, back when I was in grad school, and actually way before that, people kind of recognized this with graphics hardware.
sentences.zh: 对，所以在过去，当我还在读研究生时，甚至在那之前很久，人们就通过图形硬件意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: And they started hacking around on using graphics APIs and GPUs to do computing that the GPUs weren't really necessarily designed for.
sentences.zh: 他们开始尝试使用图形 API 和 GPU 来做一些 GPU 并不一定专为之设计的计算。

sentences.en: And so this is something that I focused on in grad school, and I called it GP-GPU, which stands for General Purpose Computation on GPUs.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在研究生期间专注的研究方向，我称之为 GP-GPU，也就是通用 GPU 计算（General Purpose Computation on GPUs）。

sentences.en: And since then, that's become something that isn't just grad students mucking around with graphics APIs.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，这就不再只是研究生们捣鼓图形 API 的玩票之作了。

sentences.en: And back in 2006 or 2007, NVIDIA launched CUDA,
sentences.zh: 在 2006 或 2007 年，英伟达推出了 CUDA，

sentences.en: which is a set of extensions to C and C++ that allow you to program GPUs for parallel computing in a traditional programming language rather than using a graphics API.
sentences.zh: 这是一套针对 C 和 C++ 的扩展，允许你使用传统编程语言为并行计算编写 GPU 程序，而不必使用图形 API。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, before...
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，在……

sentences.en: Oh, go ahead, Patrick.
sentences.zh: 哦，请讲，帕特里克。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I kind of recall vaguely that time when people first started kind of doing the GP-GPU stuff.
sentences.zh: 对，我还隐约记得人们刚开始搞 GP-GPU 那会儿。

sentences.en: And, I mean, you might be able to fill me in where I'm misremembering or incorrect, Mark, but at first you were writing in a language which was essentially a shader for the GPUs.
sentences.zh: 马克，如果我记忆有误或说得不对，你大可以纠正我，但一开始你写的是一种本质上是 GPU 着色器的语言。

sentences.en: So you kind of had to still frame whatever problem you were doing in terms of trying to tell the graphics what to do.
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上还得把你要解决的任何问题，都框定在如何指挥图形硬件去运作的范畴内。

sentences.en: Then CUDA came out.
sentences.zh: 然后 CUDA 就问世了。

sentences.en: What was that process like, and what did NVIDIA really see that made them say, hey, there's something here?
sentences.zh: 那个过程是怎样的？英伟达究竟看到了什么，才让他们说出“嘿，这块有搞头”？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有意思。

sentences.en: So my personal story for this was that I was an intern at NVIDIA in 2001, and that's when I sort of learned.
sentences.zh: 我个人的经历是，我在 2001 年是英伟达的一名实习生，正是在那里我了解到了这些。

sentences.en: My PhD was on cloud simulation and rendering.
sentences.zh: 我的博士论文研究的是云模拟与渲染。

sentences.en: So this was before people were talking about the cloud, so I was rendering clouds, right, like pictures of clouds.
sentences.zh: 所以这是在人们开始谈论“云计算”之前，我渲染的是云，对吧，也就是云的图像。

sentences.en: Like clouds of moisture.
sentences.zh: 就像水汽形成的云。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: In the sky.
sentences.zh: 天上的云。

sentences.en: And I had gotten this, at NVIDIA I learned from some of the engineers there about some of the things they'd done with shaders.
sentences.zh: 我当时在英伟达向那里的几位工程师了解了他们用着色器做的一些事情。

sentences.en: Like one of the guys wrote some shallow water equation solvers in DirectX and the game of life.
sentences.zh: 比如其中一个家伙在 DirectX 里写了一些浅水方程求解器和生命游戏。

sentences.en: He had the game of life running in pixel shaders.
sentences.zh: 他竟然让生命游戏在像素着色器里跑起来了。

sentences.en: And this was before, I think they called it shader model 2.0 or something like that.
sentences.zh: 这还是在，我想他们当时叫它着色器模型 2.0（Shader Model 2.0）或类似的东西之前。

sentences.en: So there was no floating point on these GPUs at that point.
sentences.zh: 所以那时这些 GPU 上还没有浮点运算。

sentences.en: So you had to kind of hack everything in fixed point.
sentences.zh: 你必须用定点数来凑合实现一切。

sentences.en: You had basically 10-bit precision in the pixel shaders.
sentences.zh: 像素着色器里基本上只有 10 位精度。

sentences.en: And that was fun.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: But I basically got the idea, and I learned that NVIDIA was going to be coming out with GPUs with floating point pixel shaders in the near future.
sentences.zh: 但我基本上萌生了一个想法，并且了解到英伟达在不久的将来会推出带有浮点像素着色器的 GPU。

sentences.en: And so I went back to grad school, and I thought, well, what if I did all of the simulation of the clouds on the GPU in addition to the rendering?
sentences.zh: 于是我回到研究生院心想，如果在渲染的同时，把云的所有模拟也都放到 GPU 上会怎么样？

sentences.en: And so I basically started doing fluid simulation on the GPU.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上开始在 GPU 上做流体模拟。

sentences.en: But I didn't know, and a bunch of other grad students and researchers were doing stuff in similar areas.
sentences.zh: 但当时我并不知道，还有一大群研究生和研究人员也在相似的领域做着研究。

sentences.en: There was ray tracing going on in shaders.
sentences.zh: 当时着色器里已经有光线追踪了。

sentences.en: There was FFTs even.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有快速傅里叶变换（FFT）。

sentences.en: And so I kind of started.
sentences.zh: 所以我差不多也就是从那时开始的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was also into the GPGP stuff very early.
sentences.zh: 对，我其实也很早就接触了 GPGP 的东西。

sentences.en: And there was a thing you could download that would do edge detection.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个可以下载的东西用来做边缘检测。

sentences.en: So instead of rendering the teapot, it would actually render the edges.
sentences.zh: 所以它不渲染茶壶，而是去渲染边缘。

sentences.en: And it was so hard.
sentences.zh: 而且太难了。

sentences.en: I mean, this was pre-Cuda.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是 Cuda 诞生之前的事。

sentences.en: It was so hard.
sentences.zh: 真的太难了。

sentences.en: I mean, it took like a week to figure out how to get it to compile.
sentences.zh: 光是弄清楚怎么把它编译成功就花了一个星期。

sentences.en: And then, oh, you don't have the right GPU.
sentences.zh: 然后，哦，你用的 GPU 不对。

sentences.en: You have to go out and buy another one.
sentences.zh: 你得出去再买一个。

sentences.en: And it was just, Cuda made it so much easier.
sentences.zh: 简直是……Cuda 让这一切变得容易太多了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think that, I mean, while I was back in grad school and not at NVIDIA before I came on full time,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，当我还回研究生院而不在英伟达、还没正式入职之前，

sentences.en: obviously people at NVIDIA really saw this opportunity.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，英伟达内部的人确实看到了这个机遇。

sentences.en: And I believe that it was Jensen, our CEO, ultimately, who was convinced.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们的 CEO 黄仁勋最终是被说服了。

sentences.en: And then by the time I got back in 2003, there was already an effort to build NV50, which became G80, which was the first Cuda-capable GPU.
sentences.zh: 等我在 2003 年返回时，公司已经在大力研发 NV50 了，也就是后来的 G80，它是第一款支持 Cuda 的 GPU。

sentences.en: And there was, you know, it was the first GPU with a dedicated computing mode with byte-addressable memory instead of just pixel shaders,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它是第一款拥有专用计算模式、配备字节可寻址内存而非仅仅是像素着色器的 GPU，

sentences.en: random access memory from the shader units.
sentences.zh: 可以从着色器单元进行随机存取内存。

sentences.en: And in terms of, you're right, it was hard.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，确实很难。

sentences.en: And it was kind of fun.
sentences.zh: 但也挺有意思的。

sentences.en: And it was, if you felt like, you know, a hacker getting this stuff to work.
sentences.zh: 而且，你会觉得自己像个极客黑客，把这些东西折腾成功了。

sentences.en: But when you got something to work, it kind of had this feeling of magic, right?
sentences.zh: 但当你的代码真的跑通时，就会有一种见证奇迹的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, wow, my fluid simulation actually works.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，我的流体模拟居然真的跑起来了。

sentences.en: Or, you know, this thing, this reaction-diffusion simulation that I wrote that really needs way more precision than I have in these fixed-point pixel shaders actually works.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，我写的这个反应扩散模拟程序，明明需要比这些定点像素着色器所能提供的精度高得多的精度，但它居然真的能运行。

sentences.en: And it felt like magic, which is really not a sustainable feeling in software development.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像魔法一样，但在软件开发中，这显然不是一种可持续的感觉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So what NVIDIA did was to build hardware that was dedicated to computing as well as graphics and then build software on top of that.
sentences.zh: 所以英伟达所做的，就是构建专为计算以及图形服务的硬件，然后在上面构建软件。

sentences.en: And so we saw early on from talking to potential customers that we would have to build something using languages that they're familiar with.
sentences.zh: 因此我们通过与潜在客户的交流很早就发现，我们必须使用他们熟悉的语言来构建产品。

sentences.en: And when we went around to customers and, you know, we were talking to people in areas ranging from defense to oil and gas
sentences.zh: 当我们拜访客户时，你知道，我们与各个领域的客户交谈，从国防到石油天然气，

sentences.en: to fluid simulation like Cadence and Affluent, I guess, was the company at the time.
sentences.zh: 再到流体力学仿真，比如 Cadence，还有 Affluent，我想那是当时那家公司的名字。

sentences.en: I think it's Ansys now.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在它叫 Ansys。

sentences.en: And they all said, well, it's got to either be Fortran.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，好吧，必须是 Fortran。

sentences.en: Some said it's got to be Fortran.
sentences.zh: 有些人说必须是 Fortran。

sentences.en: Some said it's got to be C or C++.
sentences.zh: 有些人说必须是 C 或 C++。

sentences.en: So we decided, we were kind of afraid of Fortran at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时对 Fortran 有点犯怵。

sentences.en: So we were like, well, we've got to build something that's based on C.
sentences.zh: 于是我们觉得，好吧，我们得构建一个基于 C 的东西。

sentences.en: And that became CUDA.
sentences.zh: 这就成了 CUDA。

sentences.en: So it's basically C with some extensions.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上就是带有某些扩展的 C 语言。

sentences.en: And it took away that magic feeling.
sentences.zh: 它消除了那种魔法般的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, when you wrote a program, it did what you thought it should do rather than, oh, maybe if I hack this this way, it'll work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当你写完一个程序，它能按你设想的那样运行，而不是“哦，也许我这么胡乱改改它就能管用了”，

sentences.en: And then it does.
sentences.zh: 然后它还真就管用了。

sentences.en: And did those first CUDA-capable GPUs, I mean, did they get widespread adoption?
sentences.zh: 那么那些首批支持 CUDA 的 GPU，我的意思是，它们得到了广泛的普及吗？

sentences.en: I mean, did NVIDIA's investment in putting in the extra work to build a compiler tool chain and all that, did that really kind of pay off?
sentences.zh: 我是说，英伟达在构建编译器工具链等方面投入的大量额外工作，真的得到回报了吗？

sentences.en: Or did it take a while?
sentences.zh: 还是说花了一段时间？

sentences.en: Well, it certainly, it definitely paid off.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它确实，绝对得到了回报。

sentences.en: But it also took a while.
sentences.zh: 但这也确实花了一段时间。

sentences.en: There was a lot of initial intereSt.
sentences.zh: 一开始大家的兴趣非常浓厚。

sentences.en: And, you know, adoption started immediately.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，普及工作立刻就开始了。

sentences.en: You know, people were using CUDA 1.0.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们当时在用 CUDA 1.0。

sentences.en: I still talk to customers who were like, yeah, I've been using CUDA since it first came out
sentences.zh: 我至今仍会遇到一些客户，他们会说：“对啊，我从 CUDA 一出来就在用了，

sentences.en: or the beta or whatever, you know, and starting to build real software with it right away.
sentences.zh: 或者从测试版就开始用了”，然后马上用它来开发真正的软件。

sentences.en: But to really call it successful and actually see real applications that people could go and buy or download that accelerate with GPUs probably took a couple of years.

sentences.en: It, you know, it faults on that memory and then a page, uh, fault handler runs and it actually loads the data into memory.

sentences.en: And then the CPU can proceed with accessing it.

sentences.en: Well, before Pascal, GPUs didn't have the ability to page fault, but we kind of, um, you know,
